extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about West Nile Virus Disease.

Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports WNV human cases as 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CDC case definitions; 'suspected' is rarely a formal category for WNV

Deaths are typically reported as WNV-associated or WNV-attributed; note if death was a contributing vs. underlying cause
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH publications — note absence if not found
ArboNET national data may lag state-level CDPH reporting by weeks — prefer CDPH for timeliness within the collection window
disambiguation_risks: 'West Nile' may co-occur with geographic references to the West Nile region of Uganda — exclude non-disease geographic references
'West Nile fever' may be confused with other febrile arboviral illnesses (e.g., dengue, Zika) in non-specific reporting
ArboNET data may aggregate multiple arboviral diseases — filter specifically for WNV
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive case classifications must be tracked separately; totals may differ by source
Cumulative vs. incident (weekly/monthly) counts must be distinguished — August 2024 data may be reported as cumulative year-to-date
County-level vs. state-level aggregation: some sources report only state totals; others provide county breakdowns
Probable vs. confirmed case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting year — note CDC vs. CDPH definitions
Dead bird and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
Sentinel chicken seroconversion data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
CDPH may publish weekly updates that are later revised in annual summaries — prefer most recent authoritative figure

count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports WNV human cases as 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CDC case definitions; 'suspected' is rarely a formal category for WNV
Neuroinvasive disease (encephalitis, meningitis, AFP) and non-neuroinvasive disease (West Nile fever) are reported as distinct subcategories — record both if available
Case counts for August 2024 may appear as cumulative year-to-date (Jan–Aug) rather than monthly incident counts — document the reporting period explicitly
Deaths are typically reported as WNV-associated or WNV-attributed; note if death was a contributing vs. underlying cause
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH publications — note absence if not found
ArboNET national data may lag state-level CDPH reporting by weeks — prefer CDPH for timeliness within the collection window
disambiguation_risks: 'West Nile' may co-occur with geographic references to the West Nile region of Uganda — exclude non-disease geographic references
'West Nile fever' may be confused with other febrile arboviral illnesses (e.g., dengue, Zika) in non-specific reporting
ArboNET data may aggregate multiple arboviral diseases — filter specifically for WNV
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive case classifications must be tracked separately; totals may differ by source
Cumulative vs. incident (weekly/monthly) counts must be distinguished — August 2024 data may be reported as cumulative year-to-date
County-level vs. state-level aggregation: some sources report only state totals; others provide county breakdowns
Probable vs. confirmed case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting year — note CDC vs. CDPH definitions
Dead bird and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
Sentinel chicken seroconversion data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
CDPH may publish weekly updates that are later revised in annual summaries — prefer most recent authoritative figure

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about West Nile Virus Disease.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports WNV human cases as 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CDC case definitions; 'suspected' is rarely a formal category for WNV
Neuroinvasive disease (encephalitis, meningitis, AFP) and non-neuroinvasive disease (West Nile fever) are reported as distinct subcategories — record both if available
Case counts for August 2024 may appear as cumulative year-to-date (Jan–Aug) rather than monthly incident counts — document the reporting period explicitly
Deaths are typically reported as WNV-associated or WNV-attributed; note if death was a contributing vs. underlying cause
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH publications — note absence if not found
ArboNET national data may lag state-level CDPH reporting by weeks — prefer CDPH for timeliness within the collection window
disambiguation_risks: 'West Nile' may co-occur with geographic references to the West Nile region of Uganda — exclude non-disease geographic references
'West Nile fever' may be confused with other febrile arboviral illnesses (e.g., dengue, Zika) in non-specific reporting
ArboNET data may aggregate multiple arboviral diseases — filter specifically for WNV
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive case classifications must be tracked separately; totals may differ by source
Cumulative vs. incident (weekly/monthly) counts must be distinguished — August 2024 data may be reported as cumulative year-to-date
County-level vs. state-level aggregation: some sources report only state totals; others provide county breakdowns
Probable vs. confirmed case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting year — note CDC vs. CDPH definitions
Dead bird and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
Sentinel chicken seroconversion data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
CDPH may publish weekly updates that are later revised in annual summaries — prefer most recent authoritative figure

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about West Nile Virus Disease.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH publishes weekly WNV surveillance summaries and county-level breakdowns; these are the primary extractable records for confirmed, probable, and neuroinvasive case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV human case data that may include California August 2024 counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify high-burden California county health department sources (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, San Bernardino, Riverside) reporting WNV human cases or deaths in August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: California's Central Valley and Southern California counties historically report the highest WNV burden; county-level reports may contain locality-specific extractable records not aggregated at the state level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases or international organization summaries (e.g., PAHO, WHO) that cross-reference California WNV human case counts for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent aggregators provide a held-back validation layer to compare against CDPH and county-level collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC Wonder, ProMED, or HealthMap structured data entries for West Nile virus in California during August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured surveillance databases and alert systems provide independently aggregated counts usable for masked validation without contaminating collection.

source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding whether reported counts are confirmed, probable, neuroinvasive, or cumulative-vs-weekly is essential for correct field mapping and normalization.

source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature may clarify clinical syndrome classifications (WNND, WNF, acute flaccid paralysis) and reporting lag patterns relevant to August 2024 data.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: California Department of Public Health (CDPH) – Division of Communicable Disease Control publishes weekly West Nile virus surveillance summaries with human case counts by county, case classification (confirmed/probable/neuroinvasive), deaths, and reporting date. This is the primary authoritative source for California WNV human data.

High-burden county health departments (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, San Bernardino, Riverside, Stanislaus, Tulare) may publish independent WNV human case reports, press releases, or dashboards with locality-level data not available in state aggregates.

CDC ArboNET (Division of Vector-Borne Diseases) publishes national WNV human case surveillance data by state, including California, with neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive breakdowns. Weekly and annual tables may cover August 2024.
PAHO and WHO situation reports may reference US/California WNV case counts as part of regional arboviral surveillance summaries, providing an independent validation layer.
Structured databases including CDC Wonder, ProMED-mail, HealthMap, and California open data portals may contain machine-readable WNV case records for California in August 2024 usable for validation.
Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on California WNV provide case definitions, syndrome classifications, and reporting methodology context essential for correct field normalization.

Reputable news outlets (LA Times, Sacramento Bee, SF Chronicle) and situation reports may publish early WNV case or death announcements citing official sources, providing collection support signals for August 2024.

query_batch.query: California West Nile virus cases deaths 2024 CDPH surveillance weekly report August
query_batch.query_rationale: CDPH publishes weekly WNV surveillance summaries during transmission season (typically May–October). This query targets the California Department of Public Health's official WNV reporting pages, which are the primary authoritative source for statewide case counts, deaths, and county-level breakdowns. 'August' and '2024' are included as unquoted terms to avoid over-constraining the query against pages that may use date ranges or cumulative language.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDPH West Nile virus surveillance bulletin or weekly update page listing case counts by county and week/month for 2024
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdph.ca.gov domain, official surveillance report language, tabular case data with county breakdowns

query_batch.query: CDC ArboNET West Nile virus California 2024 cases neuroinvasive fever deaths statistics
query_batch.query_rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV case counts including neuroinvasive disease, fever cases, and deaths. CDC's WNV statistics page is updated periodically and provides confirmed/probable breakdowns by state. This serves as a cross-validation source against CDPH data and may include August 2024 cumulative or monthly figures.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC WNV statistics page or ArboNET data table showing California 2024 case counts by disease category (neuroinvasive, fever) and deaths
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain, ArboNET attribution, tabular state-level data

query_batch.query: West Nile virus August 2024 California county cases deaths "Los Angeles" OR "Sacramento" OR "Kern" OR "Fresno" health department
query_batch.query_rationale: California WNV burden is concentrated in the Central Valley and Southern California. Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, and Fresno counties historically report the highest WNV case counts. County health departments often publish their own press releases or surveillance updates with locality-level data not disaggregated in state reports. This query targets those sub-state sources to populate the 'locality' field.

CDC ArboNET (Division of Vector-Borne Diseases) publishes national WNV human case surveillance data by state, including California, with neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive breakdowns. Weekly and annual tables may cover August 2024.
PAHO and WHO situation reports may reference US/California WNV case counts as part of regional arboviral surveillance summaries, providing an independent validation layer.
Structured databases including CDC Wonder, ProMED-mail, HealthMap, and California open data portals may contain machine-readable WNV case records for California in August 2024 usable for validation.
Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on California WNV provide case definitions, syndrome classifications, and reporting methodology context essential for correct field normalization.

Reputable news outlets (LA Times, Sacramento Bee, SF Chronicle) and situation reports may publish early WNV case or death announcements citing official sources, providing collection support signals for August 2024.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports WNV human cases as 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CDC case definitions; 'suspected' is rarely a formal category for WNV
Neuroinvasive disease (encephalitis, meningitis, AFP) and non-neuroinvasive disease (West Nile fever) are reported as distinct subcategories — record both if available
Case counts for August 2024 may appear as cumulative year-to-date (Jan–Aug) rather than monthly incident counts — document the reporting period explicitly
Deaths are typically reported as WNV-associated or WNV-attributed; note if death was a contributing vs. underlying cause
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH publications — note absence if not found
ArboNET national data may lag state-level CDPH reporting by weeks — prefer CDPH for timeliness within the collection window
disambiguation_risks: 'West Nile' may co-occur with geographic references to the West Nile region of Uganda — exclude non-disease geographic references
'West Nile fever' may be confused with other febrile arboviral illnesses (e.g., dengue, Zika) in non-specific reporting
ArboNET data may aggregate multiple arboviral diseases — filter specifically for WNV
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive case classifications must be tracked separately; totals may differ by source
Cumulative vs. incident (weekly/monthly) counts must be distinguished — August 2024 data may be reported as cumulative year-to-date
County-level vs. state-level aggregation: some sources report only state totals; others provide county breakdowns
Probable vs. confirmed case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting year — note CDC vs. CDPH definitions
Dead bird and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
Sentinel chicken seroconversion data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
CDPH may publish weekly updates that are later revised in annual summaries — prefer most recent authoritative figure

count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports WNV human cases as 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CDC case definitions; 'suspected' is rarely a formal category for WNV
Neuroinvasive disease (encephalitis, meningitis, AFP) and non-neuroinvasive disease (West Nile fever) are reported as distinct subcategories — record both if available
Case counts for August 2024 may appear as cumulative year-to-date (Jan–Aug) rather than monthly incident counts — document the reporting period explicitly
Deaths are typically reported as WNV-associated or WNV-attributed; note if death was a contributing vs. underlying cause
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH publications — note absence if not found
ArboNET national data may lag state-level CDPH reporting by weeks — prefer CDPH for timeliness within the collection window
disambiguation_risks: 'West Nile' may co-occur with geographic references to the West Nile region of Uganda — exclude non-disease geographic references
'West Nile fever' may be confused with other febrile arboviral illnesses (e.g., dengue, Zika) in non-specific reporting
ArboNET data may aggregate multiple arboviral diseases — filter specifically for WNV
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive case classifications must be tracked separately; totals may differ by source
Cumulative vs. incident (weekly/monthly) counts must be distinguished — August 2024 data may be reported as cumulative year-to-date
County-level vs. state-level aggregation: some sources report only state totals; others provide county breakdowns
Probable vs. confirmed case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting year — note CDC vs. CDPH definitions
Dead bird and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
Sentinel chicken seroconversion data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
CDPH may publish weekly updates that are later revised in annual summaries — prefer most recent authoritative figure

count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports WNV human cases as 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CDC case definitions; 'suspected' is rarely a formal category for WNV
Neuroinvasive disease (encephalitis, meningitis, AFP) and non-neuroinvasive disease (West Nile fever) are reported as distinct subcategories — record both if available
Case counts for August 2024 may appear as cumulative year-to-date (Jan–Aug) rather than monthly incident counts — document the reporting period explicitly
Deaths are typically reported as WNV-associated or WNV-attributed; note if death was a contributing vs. underlying cause
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH publications — note absence if not found
ArboNET national data may lag state-level CDPH reporting by weeks — prefer CDPH for timeliness within the collection window
disambiguation_risks: 'West Nile' may co-occur with geographic references to the West Nile region of Uganda — exclude non-disease geographic references
'West Nile fever' may be confused with other febrile arboviral illnesses (e.g., dengue, Zika) in non-specific reporting
ArboNET data may aggregate multiple arboviral diseases — filter specifically for WNV
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive case classifications must be tracked separately; totals may differ by source
Cumulative vs. incident (weekly/monthly) counts must be distinguished — August 2024 data may be reported as cumulative year-to-date
County-level vs. state-level aggregation: some sources report only state totals; others provide county breakdowns
Probable vs. confirmed case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting year — note CDC vs. CDPH definitions
Dead bird and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
Sentinel chicken seroconversion data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
CDPH may publish weekly updates that are later revised in annual summaries — prefer most recent authoritative figure

query_batch.query: California West Nile virus cases deaths 2024 CDPH surveillance weekly report August
query_batch.query_rationale: CDPH publishes weekly WNV surveillance summaries during transmission season (typically May–October). This query targets the California Department of Public Health's official WNV reporting pages, which are the primary authoritative source for statewide case counts, deaths, and county-level breakdowns. 'August' and '2024' are included as unquoted terms to avoid over-constraining the query against pages that may use date ranges or cumulative language.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDPH West Nile virus surveillance bulletin or weekly update page listing case counts by county and week/month for 2024
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdph.ca.gov domain, official surveillance report language, tabular case data with county breakdowns

query_batch.query: CDC ArboNET West Nile virus California 2024 cases neuroinvasive fever deaths statistics
query_batch.query_rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV case counts including neuroinvasive disease, fever cases, and deaths. CDC's WNV statistics page is updated periodically and provides confirmed/probable breakdowns by state. This serves as a cross-validation source against CDPH data and may include August 2024 cumulative or monthly figures.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC WNV statistics page or ArboNET data table showing California 2024 case counts by disease category (neuroinvasive, fever) and deaths
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain, ArboNET attribution, tabular state-level data

query_batch.query: West Nile virus August 2024 California county cases deaths "Los Angeles" OR "Sacramento" OR "Kern" OR "Fresno" health department
query_batch.query_rationale: California WNV burden is concentrated in the Central Valley and Southern California. Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, and Fresno counties historically report the highest WNV case counts. County health departments often publish their own press releases or surveillance updates with locality-level data not disaggregated in state reports. This query targets those sub-state sources to populate the 'locality' field.

query_batch.expected_trust_signal: lacounty.gov, saccounty.gov, kernpublichealth.com, or similar county health domain; official press release format

iterative_search_queries.query: California West Nile virus cases deaths 2024 CDPH surveillance weekly report August
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: CDPH publishes weekly WNV surveillance summaries during transmission season (typically May–October). This query targets the California Department of Public Health's official WNV reporting pages, which are the primary authoritative source for statewide case counts, deaths, and county-level breakdowns. 'August' and '2024' are included as unquoted terms to avoid over-constraining the query against pages that may use date ranges or cumulative language.

iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: cdph.ca.gov domain, official surveillance report language, tabular case data with county breakdowns

iterative_search_queries.query: CDC ArboNET West Nile virus California 2024 cases neuroinvasive fever deaths statistics
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV case counts including neuroinvasive disease, fever cases, and deaths. CDC's WNV statistics page is updated periodically and provides confirmed/probable breakdowns by state. This serves as a cross-validation source against CDPH data and may include August 2024 cumulative or monthly figures.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC WNV statistics page or ArboNET data table showing California 2024 case counts by disease category (neuroinvasive, fever) and deaths
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain, ArboNET attribution, tabular state-level data

iterative_search_queries.query: West Nile virus August 2024 California county cases deaths "Los Angeles" OR "Sacramento" OR "Kern" OR "Fresno" health department
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: California WNV burden is concentrated in the Central Valley and Southern California. Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, and Fresno counties historically report the highest WNV case counts. County health departments often publish their own press releases or surveillance updates with locality-level data not disaggregated in state reports. This query targets those sub-state sources to populate the 'locality' field.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: County public health department press release, advisory, or surveillance update reporting WNV cases or deaths in August 2024 with specific locality or zip code data
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: lacounty.gov, saccounty.gov, kernpublichealth.com, or similar county health domain; official press release format

iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: Publication date in August 2024; quotes attributed to CDPH, county health officer, or official spokesperson; numeric case/death figures

count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports WNV human cases as 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CDC case definitions; 'suspected' is rarely a formal category for WNV
Neuroinvasive disease (encephalitis, meningitis, AFP) and non-neuroinvasive disease (West Nile fever) are reported as distinct subcategories — record both if available
Case counts for August 2024 may appear as cumulative year-to-date (Jan–Aug) rather than monthly incident counts — document the reporting period explicitly
Deaths are typically reported as WNV-associated or WNV-attributed; note if death was a contributing vs. underlying cause
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH publications — note absence if not found
ArboNET national data may lag state-level CDPH reporting by weeks — prefer CDPH for timeliness within the collection window
disambiguation_risks: 'West Nile' may co-occur with geographic references to the West Nile region of Uganda — exclude non-disease geographic references
'West Nile fever' may be confused with other febrile arboviral illnesses (e.g., dengue, Zika) in non-specific reporting
ArboNET data may aggregate multiple arboviral diseases — filter specifically for WNV
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive case classifications must be tracked separately; totals may differ by source
Cumulative vs. incident (weekly/monthly) counts must be distinguished — August 2024 data may be reported as cumulative year-to-date
County-level vs. state-level aggregation: some sources report only state totals; others provide county breakdowns
Probable vs. confirmed case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting year — note CDC vs. CDPH definitions
Dead bird and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
Sentinel chicken seroconversion data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
CDPH may publish weekly updates that are later revised in annual summaries — prefer most recent authoritative figure

count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports WNV human cases as 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CDC case definitions; 'suspected' is rarely a formal category for WNV
Neuroinvasive disease (encephalitis, meningitis, AFP) and non-neuroinvasive disease (West Nile fever) are reported as distinct subcategories — record both if available
Case counts for August 2024 may appear as cumulative year-to-date (Jan–Aug) rather than monthly incident counts — document the reporting period explicitly
Deaths are typically reported as WNV-associated or WNV-attributed; note if death was a contributing vs. underlying cause
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH publications — note absence if not found
ArboNET national data may lag state-level CDPH reporting by weeks — prefer CDPH for timeliness within the collection window
disambiguation_risks: 'West Nile' may co-occur with geographic references to the West Nile region of Uganda — exclude non-disease geographic references
'West Nile fever' may be confused with other febrile arboviral illnesses (e.g., dengue, Zika) in non-specific reporting
ArboNET data may aggregate multiple arboviral diseases — filter specifically for WNV
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive case classifications must be tracked separately; totals may differ by source
Cumulative vs. incident (weekly/monthly) counts must be distinguished — August 2024 data may be reported as cumulative year-to-date
County-level vs. state-level aggregation: some sources report only state totals; others provide county breakdowns
Probable vs. confirmed case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting year — note CDC vs. CDPH definitions
Dead bird and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
Sentinel chicken seroconversion data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
CDPH may publish weekly updates that are later revised in annual summaries — prefer most recent authoritative figure

All CDPH/westnile.ca.gov figures are cumulative year-to-date, not calendar-month specific. August 2024 case counts must be derived by identifying the weekly reports dated within 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31 and reading the cumulative totals at the start and end of that window.

Facebook.com results (4 accepted candidates) should not be used as primary evidence sources. They are social media reposts and lack direct traceability to original CDPH press release URLs.

The CDC historic data page (1999-2025) is the correct federal source for 2024 California annual totals.

Sacramento County and Kern County health department sources did not surface as accepted candidates despite targeted queries. These gaps may require direct navigation to saccounty.gov and kernpublichealth.com at the data extraction stage.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports WNV human cases as 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CDC case definitions; 'suspected' is rarely a formal category for WNV
Neuroinvasive disease (encephalitis, meningitis, AFP) and non-neuroinvasive disease (West Nile fever) are reported as distinct subcategories — record both if available
Case counts for August 2024 may appear as cumulative year-to-date (Jan–Aug) rather than monthly incident counts — document the reporting period explicitly
Deaths are typically reported as WNV-associated or WNV-attributed; note if death was a contributing vs. underlying cause
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH publications — note absence if not found
ArboNET national data may lag state-level CDPH reporting by weeks — prefer CDPH for timeliness within the collection window
disambiguation_risks: 'West Nile' may co-occur with geographic references to the West Nile region of Uganda — exclude non-disease geographic references
'West Nile fever' may be confused with other febrile arboviral illnesses (e.g., dengue, Zika) in non-specific reporting
ArboNET data may aggregate multiple arboviral diseases — filter specifically for WNV
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive case classifications must be tracked separately; totals may differ by source
Cumulative vs. incident (weekly/monthly) counts must be distinguished — August 2024 data may be reported as cumulative year-to-date
County-level vs. state-level aggregation: some sources report only state totals; others provide county breakdowns
Probable vs. confirmed case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting year — note CDC vs. CDPH definitions
Dead bird and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
Sentinel chicken seroconversion data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
CDPH may publish weekly updates that are later revised in annual summaries — prefer most recent authoritative figure

Facebook.com results (4 accepted candidates) should not be used as primary evidence sources. They are social media reposts and lack direct traceability to original CDPH press release URLs.

The CDC historic data page (1999-2025) is the correct federal source for 2024 California annual totals.

Probable vs. confirmed case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting year — note CDC vs. CDPH definitions
Dead bird and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate

iterative_search_queries.query: CDC West Nile virus 2024 provisional data cases deaths California neuroinvasive non-neuroinvasive
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Iteration 1 found the CDC ArboNET historic data page (1999–2025 aggregates) but not the 2024 provisional/current-year statistics page, which CDC typically publishes separately during and after the transmission season. The 2024 provisional page would show California-specific neuroinvasive disease cases, non-neuroinvasive (fever) cases, and deaths for 2024, serving as a federal cross-validation source. This query targets that distinct CDC page.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC WNV 2024 provisional statistics page showing state-level case counts (neuroinvasive, non-neuroinvasive) and deaths for California, with 'provisional' or 'preliminary' language
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain; page title referencing '2024' and 'provisional' or 'statistics'; tabular state-level data with California row
iterative_search_queries.previous_iteration_basis: iter1_q2 — CDC historic data page found but 2024 provisional page not yet surfaced

iterative_search_queries.query: West Nile virus August 2024 California deaths confirmed CDPH press release Sacramento Kern Fresno
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Deaths are the most critical unfilled field for August 2024. The Facebook snippet from iteration 1 referenced a CDPH press release confirming 'first human West Nile virus deaths' but was undated and from a low-trust domain. This query targets CDPH press releases and Sacramento/Kern/Fresno county health department pages that would confirm deaths and case counts in August 2024. These counties are historically the highest-burden WNV counties in California outside of LA.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDPH press release or official advisory confirming WNV deaths in California in August 2024; Sacramento County, Kern County, or Fresno County health department WNV update with case counts and deaths for August 2024
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: cdph.ca.gov, saccounty.gov, kernpublichealth.com, or fresnocountyca.gov domain; press release format with date in August 2024; numeric death and case figures attributed to official spokesperson
iterative_search_queries.previous_iteration_basis: iter1_q3 — county-level sources for Sacramento, Kern, Fresno not found; deaths field unfilled

count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports WNV human cases as 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CDC case definitions; 'suspected' is rarely a formal category for WNV
Neuroinvasive disease (encephalitis, meningitis, AFP) and non-neuroinvasive disease (West Nile fever) are reported as distinct subcategories — record both if available
Case counts for August 2024 may appear as cumulative year-to-date (Jan–Aug) rather than monthly incident counts — document the reporting period explicitly
Deaths are typically reported as WNV-associated or WNV-attributed; note if death was a contributing vs. underlying cause
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH publications — note absence if not found
ArboNET national data may lag state-level CDPH reporting by weeks — prefer CDPH for timeliness within the collection window
disambiguation_risks: 'West Nile' may co-occur with geographic references to the West Nile region of Uganda — exclude non-disease geographic references
'West Nile fever' may be confused with other febrile arboviral illnesses (e.g., dengue, Zika) in non-specific reporting
ArboNET data may aggregate multiple arboviral diseases — filter specifically for WNV
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive case classifications must be tracked separately; totals may differ by source
Cumulative vs. incident (weekly/monthly) counts must be distinguished — August 2024 data may be reported as cumulative year-to-date
County-level vs. state-level aggregation: some sources report only state totals; others provide county breakdowns
Probable vs. confirmed case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting year — note CDC vs. CDPH definitions
Dead bird and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
Sentinel chicken seroconversion data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
CDPH may publish weekly updates that are later revised in annual summaries — prefer most recent authoritative figure

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: California Department of Public Health (CDPH) – Division of Communicable Disease Control publishes weekly West Nile virus surveillance summaries with human case counts by county, case classification (confirmed/probable/neuroinvasive), deaths, and reporting date. count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports WNV human cases as 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CDC case definitions; 'suspected' is rarely a formal category for WNV
Neuroinvasive disease (encephalitis, meningitis, AFP) and non-neuroinvasive disease (West Nile fever) are reported as distinct subcategories — record both if available
Case counts for August 2024 may appear as cumulative year-to-date (Jan–Aug) rather than monthly incident counts — document the reporting period explicitly
Deaths are typically reported as WNV-associated or WNV-attributed; note if death was a contributing vs. underlying cause
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH publications — note absence if not found
ArboNET national data may lag state-level CDPH reporting by weeks — prefer CDPH for timeliness within the collection window
disambiguation_risks: 'West Nile' may co-occur with geographic references to the West Nile region of Uganda — exclude non-disease geographic references
'West Nile fever' may be confused with other febrile arboviral illnesses (e.g., dengue, Zika) in non-specific reporting
ArboNET data may aggregate multiple arboviral diseases — filter specifically for WNV
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive case classifications must be tracked separately; totals may differ by source
Cumulative vs. incident (weekly/monthly) counts must be distinguished — August 2024 data may be reported as cumulative year-to-date
County-level vs. state-level aggregation: some sources report only state totals; others provide county breakdowns
Probable vs. confirmed case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting year — note CDC vs. CDPH definitions
Dead bird and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
Sentinel chicken seroconversion data are NOT human case counts — do not conflate
CDPH may publish weekly updates that are later revised in annual summaries — prefer most recent authoritative figure

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: California Department of Public Health (CDPH) – Division of Communicable Disease Control publishes weekly West Nile virus surveillance summaries with human case counts by county, case classification (confirmed/probable/neuroinvasive), deaths, and reporting date. This is the primary authoritative source for California WNV human data.

High-burden county health departments (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, San Bernardino, Riverside, Stanislaus, Tulare) may publish independent WNV human case reports, press releases, or dashboards with locality-level data not available in state aggregates.

CDC ArboNET (Division of Vector-Borne Diseases) publishes national WNV human case surveillance data by state, including California, with neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive breakdowns. Weekly and annual tables may cover August 2024.
PAHO and WHO situation reports may reference US/California WNV case counts as part of regional arboviral surveillance summaries, providing an independent validation layer.
Structured databases including CDC Wonder, ProMED-mail, HealthMap, and California open data portals may contain machine-readable WNV case records for California in August 2024 usable for validation.
Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on California WNV provide case definitions, syndrome classifications, and reporting methodology context essential for correct field normalization.

Reputable news outlets (LA Times, Sacramento Bee, SF Chronicle) and situation reports may publish early WNV case or death announcements citing official sources, providing collection support signals for August 2024.

likely_reporting_agencies: California Department of Public Health (CDPH) – Division of Communicable Disease Control
County/Local Health Departments (e.g., Los Angeles County DPH, Sacramento County DHHS, Kern County Public Health, Fresno County DPH, San Bernardino County DPH, Riverside County DPH)

Mosquito and Vector Control Association of California (MVCAC)

disease_intelligence.suggested_geographic_granularity: ["state (California)", "county (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, San Bernardino, Riverside, Stanislaus, Tulare)", "region (e.g., Central Valley, Southern California, Bay Area)"]
disease_intelligence.suggested_time_granularity: ["weekly (CDPH publishes weekly WNV updates during transmission season)", "monthly (August 2024 incident or cumulative-to-August)", "annual (2024 year-to-date cumulative)"]
count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports WNV human cases as 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CDC case definitions; 'suspected' is rarely a formal category for WNV
Neuroinvasive disease (encephalitis, meningitis, AFP) and non-neuroinvasive disease (West Nile fever) are reported as distinct subcategories — record both if available
Case counts for August 2024 may appear as cumulative year-to-date (Jan–Aug) rather than monthly incident counts — document the reporting period explicitly
Deaths are typically reported as WNV-associated or WNV-attributed; note if death was a contributing vs. underlying cause
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH publications — note absence if not found
ArboNET national data may lag state-level CDPH reporting by weeks — prefer CDPH for timeliness within the collection window
disambiguation_risks: 'West Nile' may co-occur with geographic references to the West Nile region of Uganda — exclude non-disease geographic references
'West Nile fever' may be confused with other febrile arboviral illnesses (e.g., dengue, Zika) in non-specific reporting
ArboNET data may aggregate multiple arboviral diseases — filter specifically for WNV
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive case classifications must be tracked separately; totals may differ by source
Cumulative vs. incident (weekly/monthly) counts must be distinguished — August 2024 data may be reported as cumulative year-to-date
